correctness.rationale: The explicit 12-vertex adjacency model yields exactly one connected 20-face triangulated closed surface with Euler characteristic 2 plus six antipodal 1-simplices absent from all triangles. The sphere and pair long exact sequence yield the integral groups and their full signed action, so there is no torsion inference from only field ranks. Exact integer boundary ranks 11 and 19 with nineteen unit Smith factors, the spherical fundamental 2-cycle and all 120 automorphism characters were independently recomputed from the bundled program.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2005 claw-free and 2010 star-cluster results provide general connectivity/topology methods, not the exact two-degree integral \(A_5\times C_2\) module of this specific independence complex. The closest indexed records and own claims concern neighborhood, three-cut, second-independence, or induced-forest complexes: none implies the present statement as a stated corollary, reduction or identical face definition. Publication-priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: An unindexed specialist account of the complement graph of the icosahedron or its six axes may express the same integral module without the term independence complex.
The MathWorld graph table and brief published-finding corpus summaries were not treated as full-text novelty certificates; possible unpublished equivalences require independent priority review.
The standard A5 character-table identification is mathematical background; no new abstract representation-theoretic theorem is asserted.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural integral equivariant homology classification for the canonical icosahedral graph. The canonical sphere/six-antipodal-edge structure explains the appearance of the signed six-axis lattice and a nontrivial six-dimensional rational A5 module, information impossible to infer from generic connectivity estimates or ordinary Betti numbers. It cleanly separates rotation-fixed and full-automorphism-fixed homology.
